title: Preflight rampdown scenario and regression drill
summary: Cross-functional preflight to rehearse a rampdown (capacity-constrained) scenario and run through a regression-detection drill. Identified 3 playbook gaps (canary metric ownership, KV cache warmup checks, and a flaky regression in batching). Agreed next steps: patch the canary dashboard, run a focused regression suite on dedicated infra, schedule a 1-hr dry run with SRE and QA next week.
action_items: Omar Gonzalez — build canary dashboard tile for 99th latency and error burst, due 2026-11-24
Evan Brooks — write regression test for batching edge case (small sequence + long prefix), due 2026-11-22
Dani Morales — add KV cache warmup assertion to preflight smoke and document on runbook, due 2026-11-20
Maya Singh — coordinate 1-hr dry run with QA/SRE (invite + agenda), due 2026-11-19
next_steps: Share rehearsal notes and the updated runbook link (doc in #launch-preflight)
Schedule the dry run: target 2026-11-19 15:00 PST
Run focused regression on Dedicated staging with realistic traffic profile
Post-mortem follow-up if rampdown reveals new regressions
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-17 14:32 UTC | Duration ~74m | Attendees: Aisha, Ben, Dani, Evan, Maya, Priya, Omar, Jenna, Samir

Auto-summary (generated): Preflight rampdown rehearsal and regression drill; primary outcome: identified canary/metric gaps and flaky batching regression; next steps assigned.

[00:00] Aisha: ok folks thanks for joining, we have a packed agenda — two hours, or actually an hour and change, sorry, 75 minutes. trying to get through rampdown scenario, a short regression drill, and action items. Maya will kick off with the checklist.

[00:22] Maya: yeah hi, quick note, doc linked in chat — https://intra.redwood/rehearsals/preflight-2026-11-17 (please use that). agenda: 1) scenario walkthrough 2) live simulation plan 3) regression test case replay 4) post-sim triage.

[00:45] Priya: high level goal — we want to be sure a 30% capacity drop (simulated) doesn't cause silent quality regressions and that fallback routing triggers before SLO burn. also want to catch any quantization/kv-cache warmup problems that only show under long prefixes.

[01:18] Ben: quick question — are we simulating region failover or simply capacity rampdown on the existing pool? that changes the routing behavior.

[01:34] Omar: we'll do a staged rampdown in the primary pool first, then force a regional fallback if needed. start simple: reduce concurrent workers by 30% over 10 minutes.

[02:05] Jenna: QA will seed the regression harness with 12 failing prompts we saw last week in nightly: two about batching, three about prefix truncation, rest are gen-flakiness. we need dedicated infra to avoid noise from other tests.

[02:30] Samir: noted, I can carve a small dedicated staging cohort that mirrors production routing. but we need to be explicit about model variants and quantization used — otherwise regression won't reproduce.

[03:10] Evan: on batching regression — I think it's that edge where very short prompts + long conversation prefix interact with continuous batching heuristics and cause token misalignment; might be a kernel selection path that picks a fallback kernel with a bug. so we should capture the stack traces and the kernel choice strings. I have a local repro but haven't pushed test yet.

[03:58] Dani: operationally, two things to verify: 1) canary metric ownership (who alerts on 99th pct spikes), 2) KV cache warmup checks — we saw cold-cache latencies spike in earlier dry runs. also need to ensure the warmup has a deterministic assertion in the preflight.

[04:30] Aisha: this is helpful. let's run the scenario: step 1 rampdown, step 2 observe latency/error behavior, step 3 force fallback to cheaper variant if thresholds hit, step 4 run regression harness during the ramp. Maya will coordinate control plane knobs.

[05:10] Maya: I'll own the control plane choreography. quick note: the runbook currently says "fallback to compat-quantized model" but doesn't state a hard latency threshold; we need concrete numbers.

[05:40] Priya: set initial trigger at 99th > 1200ms sustained for 2 minutes, or error rate > 1% over 1 minute. that should be conservative.

[06:12] Ben: who is on alert for that? SE or oncall?

[06:22] Dani: oncall gets paging for infra-level errors but product wants to be notified earlier — suggest a composite alert to both PagerDuty and #launch-preflight channel with a runbook link.

[06:45] Omar: I'll add the composite alert rule. action: create Grafana tile combining 99th latency, error burst, and model variant fallback count.

[07:10] Evan: for debugging, add a trace header to capture kernel selection and quantization path — we've had misreported kernel names in traces before (transcription: "kernel 3b fallback vs kernel three bee"), so ensure trace schema has clear fields.

[07:46] Aisha: ok moving to regression drill. Jenna, can you run through the top two failure patterns?

[08:05] Jenna: sure, pattern A: batching edge — sometimes tokens are off by one after batching boundary when prefix length > 4096; pattern B: prefix-truncation where the model loses slot alignment after a forced truncate. both are intermittent. we can reproduce 6/10 times locally.

[08:40] Evan: the off-by-one smells like KV cache index mis-shift — when kernel fallback occurs mid-request, the cached KV pointers don't realign. need to log KV pointer offsets.

[09:05] Samir: that implies a change in our runtime's eviction/warmup order. we should add an assertion that after kernel fallback the KV cache base index equals expected value. Dani can add that as a smoke check.

[09:38] Dani: yep I can do that. small caveat: adding heavy assertions increases overhead in preflight; keep them lightweight.

[10:05] Maya: timeline — we want the dry run next Thursday (2026-11-19) 15:00 PST. who can't make it?

[10:20] Ben: fine. Evan: TBD but will try. Jenna: yes. Omar: yes.

[10:40] Aisha: good. Now simulating the actual rampdown: Omar, can you describe the run steps?

[11:00] Omar: step 0: baseline traffic capture for 10 minutes; step 1: reduce worker pool by 10% every 2 minutes until 30%; step 2: at each increment we run a 5-minute regression burst; step 3: if threshold triggers fallback, measure failover time and observe output quality delta. We will annotate runs with event IDs so we can correlate traces.

[11:48] Priya: make sure we capture token-level diffs for the regression inputs — automated diffing and human spot-check for semantic regressions.

[12:15] Evan: we should also snapshot KV cache hit rates and prefix-sharing stats. I want to see if shared-prefix batching affects hit rates during rampdown.

[12:40] Dani: ops note: SLO burn visualization should be visible in the canary dashboard. current dashboard doesn't show fallback counts. Omar — that's on you.

[13:05] Omar: noted, I'll add fallback counts and a quick latency histogram for pre/post fallback.

[13:30] Aisha: we also discussed a possible silent-quality regression where cost-optimized variant returns good perplexity but worse instruction-following. we need to include correctness checks in the regression suite, not just token-level metrics. Jenna — can you add 3 instruction-following checks to the suite?

[13:58] Jenna: yes. I'll add prompts with gold-labels and a lightweight scorer. if scoring fails, it triggers a human review.

[14:20] Priya: small policy question — if fallback triggers during peak we prefer graceful degradation vs abrupt switch. should we implement traffic split rather than full-failover?

[14:45] Ben: that requires router changes; current router supports percentage splits but our fallback policy is binary. would need a quick rollout. Not sure we can bake that in for this release.

[15:05] Aisha: decision — for the drill we will stick to binary fallback (current behavior). we will track the human impact and consider traffic-split change in the next sprint.

[15:28] Evan: back to the flaky batching regression — I will push a targeted test and a patch candidate. action: Evan will open PR with test + instrumentation by EOD Monday.

[15:45] Dani: I'll add the KV warmup assertion to smoke and update the runbook section: preflight->warmup checks. also add a quick checklist item: "verify canary dashboard tile present and visible to product ops."

[16:05] Maya: I will update the runbook and post to #launch-preflight. attaching the doc now.

[16:25] Aisha: let's do a quick dry-run of the communication plan: if 99th > 1200ms for 2 minutes, Omar's composite alert fires. Omar, you page oncall and post to channel. Product Ops (Maya) will triage and decide if we abort ramp. Any objections?

[16:48] Omar: no objections.

[17:05] Priya: one last item — export the rehearsal output as a CSV with timestamps and event IDs for post-mortem automation. Samir can add generator.

[17:20] Samir: I'll add the CSV exporter; it will include job counts, fallback events, kernel tags.

[17:35] Aisha: ok recap. Action owners: Omar (dashboard + composite alert), Evan (PR + regression test), Dani (KV warmup assertion + runbook updates), Maya (dry-run scheduling + runbook post), Jenna (regression suite additions), Samir (CSV exporter). Dry run target 2026-11-19 15:00 PST.

[17:58] Ben: anything else?

[18:05] Evan: minor — instrument kernel string to avoid mis-parsing (we've had traces that say "kernel three b" and confusion).

[18:22] Aisha: good call. ok thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.

Post-meeting notes: brief flakiness logs attached in doc; Jenna will run a triage on intermittent failures and report back at dry run.

References and links mentioned: doc: https://intra.redwood/rehearsals/preflight-2026-11-17, runbook: https://intra.redwood/runbooks/launch-preflight, qa-harness: https://ci.redwood/testruns/regen-2026-11 (access controlled).

Caveats in transcription: occasional speaker mislabels and noise. some technical terms may be transcribed (e.g., KV cache, kernel names) with small errors.
